name: San Juan Colorado Mixtec
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: SIL Diccionario mixteco de San Juan Colorado (archive.org mixtecosanjuancoloradodiccionario) read: marks tone only (acento agudo/grave = tone), no stress statement

new_statements.quote: La mayoría de las palabras del mixteco son de dos sílabas y la primera de éstas es la tónica. Algunas palabras constan de una consonante seguida de vocal doble. Se considera que las palabras con vocal doble son de dos sílabas. La primera sílaba consta de una consonante más una vocal, mientras que la segunda sílaba consta de una sola vocal. [...] 0.2. Los tonos. Las palabras mixtecas se diferencian de las palabras castellanas en que cada sílaba tiene su propio tono. Hay tres tonos distintos, que son: alto, medio, y bajo.
new_statements.translation: Most Mixtec words have two syllables, and the first of these is the stressed (tonic) one. Some words consist of a consonant followed by a double vowel. Words with a double vowel are considered to have two syllables: the first syllable consists of a consonant plus a vowel, while the second consists of a vowel alone. [...] 0.2 Tones. Mixtec words differ from Spanish words in that every syllable has its own tone. There are three distinct tones: high, mid and low.
new_statements.citation: Stark Campbell, Sara, Andrea Johnson Peterson y Filiberto Lorenzo Cruz (comps.). 1986. Diccionario mixteco de San Juan Colorado. (Serie de vocabularios y diccionarios indígenas "Mariano Silva y Aceves" 29.) México, D.F.: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano.
new_statements.locator: Tercera parte 'La gramática mixteca', 0. La fonología, sec. 0.1.10 'Las vocales dobles' and sec. 0.2 'Los tonos', printed p. 147 (PDF p. 160)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (225 pp. archive.org facsimile, image-only) + archive.org scanned). I rendered PDF p. 160 (printed p. 147, running head 'LA FONOLOGIA 0.2') and read it as an image: sec. '0.1.10. Las vocales dobles' reads exactly 'La mayoria de las palabras del mixteco son de dos silabas y la primera de estas es la tonica. Algunas palabras constan de una consonante seguida de vocal doble. Se considera que las palabras con vocal doble son de dos silabas. La primera silaba consta de una consonante mas una vocal, mientras que la segunda silaba consta de una sola vocal. Notese los siguientes ejemplos: saa pajaro, tsaa nuevo', followed by '0.2. Los tonos:... cada silaba tiene su propio tono. Hay tr…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In the canonical disyllabic word (the Mixtec couplet, including CVV words analysed as CV.V), stress falls on the first syllable, i.e. the penultimate syllable / couplet-initial syllable; the language additionally has three contrastive level tones (high, mid, low) on every syllable, written with acute/grave accents (accents mark tone, not stress).
new_statements.exceptions: None concerning stress. The sketch says nothing about words longer than two syllables (prefixed verbs, compounds) or enclitics; it separately notes (0.2.4, pp. 148-149) that in medio-alto words whose first syllable ends in h the first vowel is lengthened (yoohó 'tú'), a lengthening that disappears when the tone changes — described as a tonal effect, not as stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement for disyllabic (couplet) words in a practical grammar sketch appended to an SIL bilingual dictionary; for disyllables 'first syllable' = penult = couplet-initial, so the reading fixed-penult is chosen on the pan-Mixtec couplet-stress interpretation (could equally be filed as couplet-initial). Tone language (3 levels); no instrumental evidence given.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes exactly 'el mixteco de San Juan Colorado, distrito de Jamiltepec, Oaxaca' (Mixteca de la Costa) = Glottolog sanj1281 / ISO mjc; authors are the SIL team for this variety (Sharon Stark = Sara Stark Campbell, Audrey F. Johnson = Andrea Johnson Peterson). No dialect mismatch.

sources.note: Grammar sec. 0.1.10 'Las vocales dobles', p. 147: most Mixtec words are disyllabic and the first syllable is the stressed one (la tónica); CVV words count as two syllables. Sec. 0.2 pp. 147-149: three level tones (alto/medio/bajo), acute/grave accents mark tone; first-syllable vowel lengthens in medio-alto words whose first syllable ends in h. The earlier scan read only the front matter (accents = tone) and missed p. 147.

sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of San Juan Colorado Mixtec (20 pp.); would supersede the one-sentence dictionary statement and likely treats stress, vowel length and tone-stress interaction explicitly. Carroll 2015 had a copy (cites it for tone), so it circulates, but it is not in SIL's public archive, archive.org, LoC or OpenLibrary — the edited volume may never have been formally distributed.
